research.text: My research focuses on statistical methodology for the social sciences. My main methodological research interests include statistical inference for social network data (longitudinal modeling, multiplex networks, relational event models, etc.) and social science and humanities data broadly (pairwise comparisons, text data, etc.). Much of my methodological work is inspired by interdisciplinary collaborations. My applied areas of interest include education, health sciences, organizational behavior, sociology, and criminology. I work in collaboration with the Gender, Relationships, and Health Lab and am part of the Digital Vaccine Project at CMU. My research has been supported by an NSF MMS Award, a Russell Sage Foundation Small Grant, and various NIH grants, amongst others.
